references.text: In [ref:Joh 3:22|John 3:22] it states that Jesus went into the Judean countryside with his disciples and stayed there with them and baptized. John 4:2 clarifies and corrects this by making clear that in reality it was not Jesus himself who baptized, but his disciples.

In [ref:Joh 3:26|John 3:26] John the Baptist's disciples say that the one who was with him on the other side of the Jordan—Jesus—is now baptizing, and everyone is coming to him. John 4:2 nuances this statement by explaining that it was the disciples, not Jesus himself, who performed the baptism.

Paul writes in [ref:1 Kor 1:14-17|1 Corinthians 1:14–17] that Christ did not send him to baptize but to preach the gospel. This reflects a similar principle as in John 4:2: Jesus himself focused on preaching and left the act of baptism to his disciples.

In [ref:Apg 10:48|Acts 10:48] Peter commands that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ, but carries it out through others. This pattern—where leaders give orders for baptism that are carried out by assistants—mirrors the practice in John 4:2 where Jesus' disciples performed the baptism on his behalf.

[ref:Joh 4:1|John 4:1] provides the immediate context, stating that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was winning and baptizing more disciples than John. Verse 2 serves as a parenthetical correction of this rumor by clarifying that it was the disciples who baptized, not Jesus himself.
